title: Israel named by Pharaoh
subtitle: The Merneptah Stele (Israel Stele)

images.caption: The upper part of Merneptah’s victory stele, from his mortuary temple at Thebes, in the Egyptian Museum, Cairo.
Detail: the name Israel (ysrỉꜣr) in line 27.

p: A large granite slab recording Pharaoh Merneptah’s victories. Near the end it lists peoples of Canaan he claims to have defeated: “Ashkelon is carried off, Gezer is seized… Israel is laid waste; his seed is not.”

It is the earliest known mention of Israel outside the Bible. The hieroglyph used marks Israel as a people rather than a city or land, which fits Israel living in the hill country of Canaan in the time of the Judges. The text is told from Egypt’s perspective. It shows that Israel was already a known people in Canaan by about 1200 BC, a fixed point for the history of Israel in the land.
